newsitem.title: UK: Med oil products firm, markets quieter, eye crude.
newsitem.headline: Med oil products firm, markets quieter, eye crude.

text.p: Mediterranean oil products were firm, taking early support from crude. A late drop in futures on Friday could exert bearish pressure.
Gasoline markets were calm and the supply/demand situation apppeared balanced.
Many players were holding back as they awaited the outcome of a U.S. military build-up in the Middle East.
Naphtha was stable. Supply was seen relatively good, with Skikda, Moroccan, Greek and Libyan material all available.
Gas oil was strong. Traders noted a fair amount of buying interest into Italy for low sulphur diesel.
No deals were reported but premiums were assessed around Oct IPE +$19/+$20, cif Genoa.
Traders said new EU low sulphur regulations looked like making North American low sulphur gas oil, arbitrage permitting, a regular feature in the Med.
On the Russian side, a cargo was reported to have traded at quotes cif high $2.25, basis Genoa. Traders said premiums were fairly steady despite rather thin Russian supply.
Physical trade in fuel oil was limited as sellers opted to hold product over the weekend and buyers held back. Prices were broadly steady in a market that looked fundementally balanced.
Interest for bunker quality was seen before the end of the month, but buyers for non-bunker spec were not highly visible. Traders said at least one ISAB cargo was still available.

Low sulphur cracked material was seen firmer with higher paper numbers. A trader looking to cover a commitment into Turkey was bidding around high $120s cif Turkey, but dealers said the party was understood to have already sourced a cargo from the U.S. and saw the market closer to $124-126 cif Med.
